Arabesque

A design system built by Arabesque Labs to set the standard for every product we make. Written for left-to-right and right-to-left alike, and designed so people get things done in the fewest steps, seeing every consequence.

Foundations

Colour

Roles, not hues: each name says what the colour is for. Every pair the system relies on is measured at build time.

Space and shape

A 4px step for everything spatial. Corners are crisp (2px); depth comes from borders and surface steps, never shadows.

Motion

Read the spec · On its own page

Steps

A numbered sequence: the stages of how something is done. Only for real sequences.

  1. 1

    Discover

    Start with the real problem, not the assumed solution. We take time to understand the constraints before writing a line of code.

  2. 2

    Design

    Structure comes before pixels. We sketch the system's shape, its data, flows and edge cases, so the build has a foundation.

  3. 3

    Build

    Small, deliberate increments instead of big-bang releases. Working software, reviewed and tested at every step.

  4. 4

    Refine

    The first version is rarely the right one. We revisit, simplify and polish until the details hold up.

Feedback

Notice and side-effect note

A message in the page, in four kinds, each with an icon and a title. A side-effect note says what else will change, before it does.

Done

Your changes are saved.

Planned maintenance

On Sunday, from 2am to 4am, saving may be slow.

Changes saved

Everyone with access can see them now.

Check your details

Some of your details may be out of date.

Couldn't load this page

The connection dropped. Check you're online, then try again.

Changing this also updates 2 related items.

Patterns

Questions and answers

The questions people ask before they start, each folded under its question, each answer short, with a link for more.

Does it work in Arabic?

Yes: every component is written for right to left as well as left to right, and every spec is in Arabic too. How right to left works

Do I need React?

No. The CSS and the small helpers in js/ work on any page; the React components write the same markup.

How is contrast checked?

The build measures every colour pair the system relies on, in both themes, and fails if any falls short.

Read the spec · On its own page

Ask, check, confirm

For anything sent, or hard to take back: ask; check errors on submit, with an error summary; let people check their answers; then confirm, with what happens next. Try submitting it empty.
